text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Paper workers' wildcat strikes in south-eastern Finland end, agreement reached in original dispute.
- Parliament constitutional committee has plans to propose a significant reduction of the President's powers.
- Centre Party chairman Esko Aho and MEP Paavo Vayrynen argued at party executive committee meeting over approaches to EMU.
- Unitas' owners lost accumulated right to 160 million markka in dividends when banking group bylaws were changed as it merged with KOP to form Merita.
- Chinese aplite granite competes with Italian carrara marble as replacement material for Finlandia Hall's decaying facade.
- Nokia more profitable than its rivals Ericsson and Motorola in 1996.
- Wholesaler Kesko says incurred virtually no losses from acquisition of Tuko and subsequent sale of most of it, but the operation tied up capital, reducing return on investment.
- State asset management company Arsenal is progressing without surprises in task to cut losses and shrink balance sheet.
- January Norscan pulp data shows Finnish producers are more flexible than Swedish and Canadian rivals.
- SEK & Grey still largest advertising agency in Finland in 1996, well ahead of second largest Hasan & Partners.
- Government proposes removing reference to God in criminal law clause on blasphemy.
- Three die as car crashes with Russian truck in southeast Finland.
- Former President Mauno Koivisto was placed in charge of removing communists from dockworkers' trade unions after the war, dissertation says.
